<!-- page 544 -->
Disposal of Stock and Equipment, Dunbow (St. Joseph's) Industrial School (Continuation of correspondence on
page I-255, Report for 1922 - 23)


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, January 3, 1924.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 28th ultimo, relative to the disposal of the assets of the St. Joseph's
(Dunbow) Indian Industrial School during the fiscal year 1922 - 23.

In reply I wish to inform you that in December, 1922, $6,026.79 was deposited in Ottawa-Trust Account No. 449. This
amount represented the proceeds from the sale of stock and equipment at the school. The Oblate Fathers and the Grey
Nuns, who were jointly interested in the management and conduct of the institution for many years, were the only
creditors of the Dunbow Industrial School with whom settlement was not made at the time of the sale. I could not
authorize the Department's Inspector to pay the arrears of salary, until such time as a statement relative to the school's
account was before me. The Indian Commissioner at Regina forwarded to me, at my request, the proceeds and the
report of our Inspector, who, made a careful audit of the school's books.

Unpaid salaries in the case of the Grey Nuns amounted to $1,225.18. This amount represents salary for several Sisters,
which was in arrears in some cases as from April 1, 1914.

With reference to the arrears of salary for the Oblate Fathers, I wish to inform you that there have been employed at
the school for many years three officers belonging to, the Order - the Principal and two lay Brothers. An Inspector's
report of some years ago shows arrears of salary owing to the Rev. Principal to be $857.29 as on April 1, 1914. When
the institution was closed in 1922, our Inspector carefully audited the books and there was found to be due to the
Oblate Fathers for salary further arrears amounting to $3,466.90, making a total in the case of the Oblate Fathers of
$4,324.19.

I trust that this explanation of cheques Nos. 8399 and 8402, drawn against Trust Account No. 449, referred to in your
letter, will be satisfactory. Enclosed you will find our Inspectors report and a covering letter from Mr. Commissioner
Graham, both of which should be returned to this Department in, due course.

I am pleased to add, for your information, that I have known for some years of the unfortunate financial condition of
the Dunbow Industrial School. Once a large, prosperous institution, the pupillage dwindled until the per capita
earnings were unable to meet the current expense. For some considerable time the church workers in charge drew only
part salary, in an effort to keep the school in a solvent condition.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, February 6, 1924.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of January 3, last, enclosing Mr. Inspector Murison's report on the
closing of the Dunbow (St. Joseph's) Industrial School.

I wish to point out that, in my opinion, the procedure followed in closing this school was not, so far as financial
matters were concerned, in strict accordance with the provisions of the Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act. Mr.
Murison disposed of the effects of the school, either by sale or by distribu-
